solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Amphibians born mostly abroad in half of great river

definitions.note: the answer is a genus name, which covers many animals, hence the plural

indicators.note: abroad means all over the place, so the letters of the word before it are scattered into a new order
taking half of a word means dropping the rest of its letters
the first part of the clue sits inside the other part, which wraps around it

blocks.note: b. is the abbreviation for born
the word itself, used as letters to rearrange
the Amazon is South America's great river

explanation.surface: Some frogs or newts are said to be born mostly overseas, in part of a mighty river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like it means 'nearly all', but it is the very word being rearranged. 'half of' keeps the front three letters of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Amblystoma is a genus of salamanders, among them the axolotl, and salamanders are amphibians.

clue.text: Earth doctor extracted from African country

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out, leaving the remainder of the longer word

blocks.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
the Gambia is a West African country

explanation.surface: A doctor is pulled out of a country in Africa, perhaps evacuated home to Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Take MB out of GAMBIA and GAIA remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaia is the Greek goddess personifying the Earth, and the name is used for the planet seen as a living whole.

clue.text: Frees parliamentarian for upper level in church

blocks.note: to clear someone is to free them, as of a charge
a Tory is a Conservative member of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is released so as to sit in a church's upper gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEARSTORY is a variant spelling of clerestory.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerestory is the upper storey of a church nave, pierced with windows above the aisle roofs.

clue.text: Stake on gee-gee coming in behindhand (but not last), …

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped from the word just before this bracketed phrase
things coming in enter another word and are wrapped by it

blocks.note: o' is a dialect contraction of on, as in o' nights
GG is the short form of gee-gee, a horse
behindhand means running late

explanation.surface: A punter puts a stake on a horse that finishes behind the field, though not quite last.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on into the next clue, whose 'One such' points back at the gee-gee. Loggats was an old game like skittles.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggat is a stake or small log thrown at a fixed stake in the old game of loggats.

clue.text: … One such, last in race, having pound on

definitions.note: refers back to the gee-gee in the clue before

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is used
one piece has the next tacked on after it

blocks.note: the final letter of race
a quid is slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Continuing the racing story: a horse comes last, with a pound bet on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One such' only makes sense with the previous clue, where a gee-gee (a horse) appears.
explanation.definitionFit: An equid is any member of the horse family, so a gee-gee is one such animal.

clue.text: What's the point of upending earth, scraping it for food?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upending turns the word upside down so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a ras is a headland or cape, which is a point of land
o' is short for of, as in o'clock
an earth is a fox's lair

explanation.surface: A gardener asks why bother turning the soil over, as birds scratch at it for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' looks like soil but is an animal's den; LAIR upended gives RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasorial birds, such as hens, habitually scratch the ground in search of food.

clue.text: Penning page, view poet's grudge

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it inside, as in a pen

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for page
a sight is a view

explanation.surface: A writer looks at a page and bears a grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poet's' signals an old poetic spelling: spight is Spenser's and Shakespeare's form of spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite is ill will or a grudge, and spight is its archaic literary spelling.

clue.text: Bum having to be persistent when denied work

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
to push is to keep pressing on
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A layabout has to keep going when refused a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as a tramp, but it is the backside. Remove OP from TO PUSH to leave TUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Tush is informal, chiefly American, slang for the buttocks, just as bum is British slang for them.

clue.text: Delicacy, bit left uneaten with section removed from goose's head

indicators.note: something removed is taken away, leaving the rest of the word
the head is the front, so the cut is made at the start of the bird's name

blocks.note: an ort is a scrap of food left over
s. is an abbreviation for section
the solan goose is the gannet

explanation.surface: A diner leaves part of a fine dish, having cut a piece off a goose's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The solan goose is the gannet; 'goose's head' reads as the bird's head but means the front of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small bunting, traditionally eaten whole in France as a prized gourmet dish.

clue.text: Entering here wronged fool gets redress

indicators.note: something entering goes inside the other piece
wronged suggests being put wrong, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: a clot is a stupid person
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool who has been wronged comes here seeking justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redress' looks like compensation, but it is read as re-dress, to dress again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclothe someone is to put clothes on them again, which is to dress them anew.

clue.text: Mum holds a party quarterly for tiny Ethiopian creature

indicators.note: a thing that holds others has them inside it

blocks.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
taken as written
a do is a party
qu. serves as a short form of quarter, here quarterly

explanation.surface: A mother throws a party every three months for a little animal from Ethiopia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarterly' is not a timetable here: it is shortened to its opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Madoqua is the genus of dik-diks, very small antelopes found in Ethiopia and East Africa.

clue.text: Head of US college accepts university process for recycling fuel?

indicators.note: something that accepts another takes it in

blocks.note: prex is American college slang for a president
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An American college president admits a university into some recycling scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of US college' looks like a first-letter instruction, but it is a single slang word for the president.
explanation.definitionFit: PUREX is the chemical method used to reprocess spent nuclear fuel, extracting plutonium and uranium for reuse.

clue.text: Holding wild gig, reverse of put-down for VIPs (7, two words)

indicators.note: a thing holding another has it inside
something wild is out of control, so the next word's letters are jumbled
the reverse of a word is that word read backwards

blocks.note: a snub is a put-down
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Important guests at a wild concert get the brush-off reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged gig goes inside after the first letter of the backwards put-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Big guns is an idiom for the most important or powerful people, the very important persons.

clue.text: Literal translator came across early female playwright's fragment of tragedy

indicators.note: a fragment is a tiny piece, here just the opening letter

blocks.note: to come across someone is to meet them
Aphra Behn (1640-89) was the first English woman to write plays professionally
the opening letter of tragedy

explanation.surface: Someone translating word for word stumbled on a scrap of a tragedy by a pioneering woman dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's of the playwright is kept as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphrast turns a text into another language word for word, rather than freely paraphrasing it.

clue.text: Sandy's extended shortened speech?

blocks.note: first meaning: Scots for long, Sandy being a stock name for a Scot
second meaning: the abbreviation for language

explanation.surface: A man named Sandy's long talk is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: The two parts are opposites in the surface, extended versus shortened, yet both give the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lang is the Scots form of long, and lang. abbreviates language, a word for speech.

clue.text: Wild canine about to die, put back in wretched quarters

indicators.note: putting a word back runs its letters in the opposite direction
about means around, so the first word surrounds the next part

blocks.note: the dhole is the Asian wild dog
to go is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: A wild dog about to die is returned to a miserable kennel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to die' reads as a phrase meaning near death; 'about' is in fact the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-hole is a squalid, mean dwelling, a place fit only for a dog.

clue.text: Recalled piece in Standard (yesterday's) no longer feared

indicators.note: a piece in the words that follow means a run of letters lifted from them
recalled suggests calling back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the end of Standard and the start of yesterday's

explanation.surface: An article from yesterday's Evening Standard, now remembered, is no longer frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' marks the answer as obsolete: ydrad is Spenser's past participle of dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Ydrad is the archaic form of dreaded, the y- prefix marking an old past participle.

clue.text: One preceding old monarch entering erred badly? should be behind

indicators.note: one thing preceding another is placed directly before it
something entering goes inside the word after it
done badly means jumbled, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ER is the royal cipher, as of Elizabeth Regina or Edward Rex
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ahead of an old king made a mistake and should have stayed behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be behind' reads as a rebuke, but 'behind' is the definition and 'should be' only joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Derrière, borrowed from French, is a polite euphemism for the buttocks, a person's behind.

clue.text: Dealer in offal distributed per tin mum's got in

indicators.note: distributed letters are spread around and dealt out in a new order
something that has got in now sits inside the rest

blocks.note: the words themselves, to be rearranged
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Offal is sold by the tin, and Mum has bought some.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give TRIPEN, with MA inserted before the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripeman sells tripe, the stomach lining of cattle, which is a kind of offal.

clue.text: One born to serve couple finding new position in Aussie tavern

indicators.note: letters finding a new position are rearranged; couple says only two of them shift

blocks.note: in Australia a hotel is the usual word for a pub

explanation.surface: A servant pair take up new jobs in an Australian pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' points at two letters: move OT from the middle of HOTEL to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf of ancient Sparta, born into the servile class, hence someone born to serve.

clue.text: Scot taking legal possession I'll have to think about

indicators.note: about means around, so the word before it is wrapped round the letter

blocks.note: taken as written
to ponder is to think

explanation.surface: A Scottish bailiff says he will need to mull it over.
explanation.walkthrough: To poind, in Scots law, is to seize goods to satisfy a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A poinder is someone who carries out a poinding, the Scottish legal seizure and sale of a debtor's goods.

clue.text: Sort of omelette, Italian, served in fat cooked with art

indicators.note: a thing served in another is placed inside it
cooked means prepared or changed, so the letters that follow are mixed

blocks.note: It. is the abbreviation for Italian
the word itself, to be rearranged
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian omelette is served cooked in fat, with some flair.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen words 'served' and 'cooked' fit the omelette so well that they pass as description rather than instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A frittata is a thick Italian omelette, usually with fillings cooked into the egg.

clue.text: Songbird, something heard circling over high place

indicators.note: a thing circling others goes all the way round them

blocks.note: a trial is a case heard in court
o. is the cricket abbreviation for over
up means in a high place

explanation.surface: A bird's song is heard as it circles above a lofty perch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something heard' sounds like a cue for a sound-alike, but it is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: The troupial is a tropical American songbird of the oriole family.

clue.text: What may be full of chocolates, some milk that one's opened

definitions.text: What may be full of chocolates

indicators.note: a thing that has been opened lets something go inside it

blocks.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk
a means one

explanation.surface: A box of chocolates sits next to a bottle of milk someone has opened.
explanation.walkthrough: PINTA comes from a 1950s British advert, 'Drinka pinta milka day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piñata is a decorated container filled with sweets and broken open at parties.

clue.text: Charged particle? what's done when opening current is switched?

indicators.note: switched means swapped round, so the two letters change places

blocks.note: AC, alternating current, standing at the start of the word
an action is a thing done; this is what follows its opening two letters

explanation.surface: A science question about charge and switching on a current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's done' is ACTION, whose first two letters are the current; turning just those round gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cation is a positively charged ion, an electrically charged particle.

clue.text: SA antelope, one in circular path, tailless

indicators.note: without a tail means the last letter is cut off
the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an orbit is a circular path

explanation.surface: A South African antelope runs round in circles and has no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: ORBIT loses its tail to give ORBI, with I placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small, slender antelope of the grasslands of southern and eastern Africa.

clue.text: Some shekels made by employee, what?

blocks.note: a man is a worker, as in management and men
eh? is a request to repeat something

explanation.surface: A worker is amazed at how many shekels he earned.
explanation.definitionFit: A maneh is an ancient Hebrew weight or sum of money equal to fifty shekels.

clue.text: Blokes with what helps to 'pull the birds', an intellectual elite

blocks.note: blokes is British slang for men
SA is sex appeal, which helps attract women (birds, in British slang)

explanation.surface: Clever men boast of their charm with women.
explanation.walkthrough: To pull is British slang for to attract romantically, and birds are young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is a society whose members must score in the top two per cent on IQ tests, a brainy elite.

clue.text: Freshly made crafted tin men won

indicators.note: something crafted is fashioned anew, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the words themselves, to be rearranged
W is the abbreviation for won in sports tables

explanation.surface: Freshly made tin soldiers won the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint-new describes something as fresh as a coin straight from the mint.

clue.text: Some silk yarn in ultramarine

indicators.note: the letters are found lying within the following word

blocks.note: the middle letters of ultramarine

explanation.surface: A skein of silk thread dyed deep blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tram is doubled silk thread used for the weft of fine fabrics.

clue.text: Wild goat seized by cheetah racing

indicators.note: the letters are held fast by the following words, lying inside them

blocks.note: across the join of cheetah and racing

explanation.surface: A goat is caught by a sprinting big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The tahr is a wild goat of the Himalayas and southern India.

clue.text: Coquille? Lucky chance catching 50

indicators.note: a thing catching another holds it inside

blocks.note: a hit is a lucky stroke
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A fluke catch of fifty, perhaps in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coquille' looks like a scallop dish, but in fencing it is the shell-shaped guard of a foil.
explanation.definitionFit: The coquille is the bell guard forming part of a sword's handle, so it is defined by example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fungus displayed by pimples, on inside

indicators.note: the word before it is placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: milia are small white skin cysts, like pimples
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fungal infection shows itself as spots on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Monilia is a genus of fungi, moulds causing brown rot in fruit.

clue.text: Favourite jar, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the solver should go by how a word is said, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: to grate is to jar on the nerves

explanation.surface: A favourite pot, as it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a pot, but it is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: Great can mean much in favour, as in being great with someone, close and well regarded.

clue.text: Fool in front of painting no longer puts blobs on?

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
places the first piece before the next
oils are paintings done in oil paint

explanation.surface: A fool before an oil painting has stopped dabbing paint on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' marks an obsolete sense, so the definition reaches past the familiar meaning of the answer, to absolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Assoil is an archaic verb meaning to soil or stain, that is, to put smudges on something.

clue.text: Street musicians moving about in damn banger (10, two words)

indicators.note: letters moving about change places, giving a new order

blocks.note: the words themselves, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Buskers wander about in a wretched old car.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for an old, battered car (it is also a sausage).
explanation.definitionFit: A German band was a group of street musicians, originally from Germany, common in Victorian Britain.
